evidence.text: A single vertical line, representing one set of ten. Analagous to the archaic characters 廿 (twenty) and 卅 (thirty).
數之具也。一爲東西，|爲南北，則四方中央備矣。凡十之屬皆从十。

Unlike 一, which was one horizontal stroke meaning one, 十 was originally simply a vertical stroke. In later forms 一 was added, forming a cross.
Possibly a pictogram (象形) for a needle, later written as 針 (OC *kjum, *kjums), borrowed phonetically for 十 (OC *ɡjub, “ten”).
Unrelated to 支, 卖, 直, 真, 德, 甫， and 七 but related to the original version of 丈 and perhaps related to 由.
The notion that 針 /针 (zhēn) belongs to the same series as 十 (shí) is not generally accepted. If they are separated, Baxter-Sagart's reconstruction can be amended to *[g][i]p.
From Proto-Sino-Tibetan *sV-ɢip.

Etymological analysis: indicative

The page presents forms labeled Shang, Western Zhou, Spring and Autumn, Warring States, and Shuowen. It reports that oracle-bone 十 is mostly a single vertical stroke, with a few examples adding a central dot; later forms added 一 to make a cross. This is a secondary collation of historical forms, not direct inspection of the original artifacts.
evidence.title: 十 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.text: The page records competing proposals: 十 as an ideographic counting mark for ten; an original graph for 針 later borrowed to write 十; and a knotted-cord or thread-joining interpretation. It does not establish the depicted object's name or pronunciation for the needle proposal. Its summarized reconstructions for 十 are Zhengzhang 2003 Old Chinese *ɡjub and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *t.[ɡ]əp; for 針 it gives *kjum/*kjums in the Zhengzhang phonetic-series table. These are system-specific reconstructions and do not independently demonstrate that the needle-name matched the borrowed numeral word.
evidence.title: 十 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.source: 說文解字, 十部 (Wikisource transcription)
evidence.text: The Han dictionary explains 十 as 數之具也 and gives a cosmological account: 一 represents east–west and 丨 north–south, completing the four directions and center. This is an attested historical explanation from the Shuowen tradition, not independent confirmation of the Shang graph's original motivation.
evidence.kind: primary historical dictionary text in modern transcription
evidence.title: 说文解字/03 - 维基文库，自由的图书馆

evidence.field: 字源字形; 字形實例
evidence.text: The character page indexes five oracle-bone forms, 36 bronze forms, Chu slips/silk forms, a Shuowen small-seal form, Qin slips, and clerical forms. It identifies listed oracle-bone examples by catalog references, including 甲870/合35260 and other 合-series identifiers. It also labels the graph 指事 and states, as its own explanatory gloss, that oracle-bone 十 represents ten with a branch, bronze forms represent a knot in cord-counting, and the later dot became a horizontal stroke. That specific branch-versus-knot interpretation is not established by the listed examples alone and conflicts with alternative analyses.
evidence.kind: dictionary character entry and form catalogue
evidence.title: 十 shí - 汉典

evidence.field: 音韻方言; local primary-reading check
evidence.text: The inspected entry gives Mandarin shí and Middle Chinese dzyip, and lists Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *t.[ɡ]əp and Zhengzhang Old Chinese *ɡjub. Supplied local primary rows independently confirm 十 as Unihan kMandarin shí and Baxter–Sagart table row 十: MC dzyip, OC *t.[g]əp, gloss “ten.” Local provenance: sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt, kMandarin row 十; sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, row 十. The Unicode Unihan character-specific URL was attempted but inaccessible in this web tool, so the local reading is not treated as externally verified evidence.
evidence.kind: dictionary phonology plus local dataset cross-check
evidence.title: 十 shí - 汉典

evidence.field: Detailed senses and dated textual examples
evidence.text: The entry separates the basic numeral sense from later or extended examples: it cites 十亩之间兮 from the Shijing, 十室九空 from Ge Hong's Baopuzi, and 十无一 from Tang writer Liu Zongyuan; it gives later citations for fractional/extent, approximate, multiplicative, ordinal, and “many/complete” uses. The page does not establish the earliest occurrence of any sense, and the apparent sequence of dictionary senses is not a chronology. The supplied record's “complete; perfect” should therefore be treated as an extension/usage, not as evidence for the graph's original meaning.
evidence.kind: dictionary senses and cited textual examples
evidence.title: 十 shí - 汉典

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Multi-function Chinese Character Database）
evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析；十字形義源流
evidence.text: The database reports oracle-bone and early bronze 十 as a vertical stroke 丨, and records several competing origin accounts: a needle-shaped graph borrowed for the numeral (attributed to 裘錫圭), a straightened stroke used to distinguish ten from 一, a staff, joined upright palms, and a knotted cord. It says some mid-Western Zhou bronze forms add a central dot, which later extends into a short horizontal stroke. These are source-reported proposals and descriptions; the database’s account does not independently establish the depicted needle’s name or pronunciation.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：十

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Multi-function Chinese Character Database）
evidence.field: 甲骨文用例；金文、戰國竹簡用例
evidence.text: The entry reports oracle-bone numeral uses including 合集1654 十月, 合集110反 奠入十 (ten turtle plastrons), and 合集29572 十牢. It also gives a bronze inscription example with 十七年 and a Warring States bamboo-slip example from 清華簡二《繫年》簡3 with 十又四年. These are reported early numeral uses, not demonstrated first attestations; the entry does not establish an early “complete/perfect” sense.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：十

evidence.text: The Shuowen entry gives 十 as 數之具也 and explains 一 as east–west and 丨 as north–south, completing four directions and the center. This is the Han dictionary’s historical explanation, not direct evidence of the graph’s original motivation.

Its original-file link resolves to https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/12/%E5%8D%81-oracle.svg. This is a modern redraw, not a photograph or direct scan of an ancient artifact.

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

search_audit.outcome: Inspected the CUHK character analysis, Wiktionary summary, Commons seal file description, and Shuowen transcription. The official Unicode page was inaccessible. A Commons search result for the exact seal-radical filename produced an internal error.

Inspected exact Commons description page and confirmed its original-file URL and CC0/public-domain notice. Direct image fetch was attempted through the Commons original-file link but returned a cache miss in the web tool.

gaps: The needle-origin proposal is not independently demonstrated: the sources inspected do not establish the name or pronunciation of the object depicted by the proposed original graph, nor an early attestation connecting that object-word to the numeral word 十. The sound comparison cannot be settled from reconstructions alone.

No character-specific oracle-bone or bronze glyph image was visually inspected. Thus the reported vertical-stroke-to-cross development relies on textual descriptions and catalog metadata, not visual examination in this research pass.

The conflicting counting-mark, cord/knot, and needle interpretations remain unresolved. The supplied dossier's single-line account is compatible with the reported early form but does not itself establish what the stroke originally depicted or whether the graph was an ideograph, pictograph, or borrowed graph.

No corpus-based earliest attestation for the numeral word, or dated earliest attestations for the extended senses “many,” “complete,” “perfect,” and “tenth,” were established. The dictionary's cited literary examples are attestations, not proof of first occurrence or semantic chronology.
A Mandarin reading for any proposed component 針 was not checked against a local exact row or an accessible official Unicode Unihan record; no component sound array should be emitted on this evidence.

Official Unicode Unihan URL https://www.unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl?codepoint=5341 was attempted twice and was inaccessible through the web tool. The supplied local row 十 = shí is recorded with its repository provenance but not represented as an inspected external Unihan page.
No extract licensing assessment was performed; the evidence used is paraphrased and character-specific, so a recurring bulk extract is not recommended from this research pass.

The earliest depicted referent remains disputed: the sources report numeral-mark, needle, staff, joined-palms, and knotted-cord proposals. The needle proposal does not establish the depicted object’s original name or pronunciation, nor a separately attested early word for that object matching the numeral word; reconstructions alone cannot prove the borrowing.

The form sequence is supported by descriptions and catalog-linked modern redrawings, but no original artifact photograph or direct paleographic catalogue record was visually inspected here. The proposed vector glyphs should be treated as modern redrawings of historical forms.

No exact earliest attestation for the numeral word is established. The reported oracle-bone numerals are early attestations, with the earliest among the examples cited here not independently dated in this research pass. The sequence of modern dictionary glosses does not establish chronology.

The supplied glosses ‘complete; perfect’ and ‘tenth’ are not evidence of their earliest use. ‘Tenth’ is seen in an oracle-bone example 十月, but this does not prove when an ordinal sense first arose. An early ‘complete/perfect’ sense was not established.

No phonetic component is proposed for 十, so no component-host sound array is warranted. The needle theory is a whole-graph borrowing hypothesis and remains unproven; it should not be conflated with a phonetic component analysis.
The official Unicode Unihan record attempt failed; local readings are retained as local-row provenance, not external verification. No exact local row for 針 was supplied or checked.

items.period: Shang period, as labeled by the source
items.tradition: Shang oracle-bone script; modern vector redraw attributed to 小學堂 record 41.EC21 (catalog note 鐵42.1合10966)
items.caption: A single vertical stroke is reported for early oracle-script forms of 十, which was used as the numeral ten. The stroke’s original referent is uncertain.
items.alt: One thick vertical black stroke with gently rounded ends, centered on a white background.
items.selection_reason: This readable form illustrates the reported early single-stroke shape associated with 十’s numeral use, without asserting what the stroke depicts.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public domain as stated on the Commons file page.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script tradition; transmitted Han-dictionary form, not a securely dated artifact image
items.tradition: Shuowen seal script; modern vector redraw attributed in part to 小學堂 record 27.5341
items.caption: 十 in a Shuowen seal-script style, drawn as a cross. Historical descriptions report that later forms added a horizontal stroke to earlier vertical-stroke forms.
items.alt: A black cross with a long vertical stroke and a shorter horizontal stroke across its center, on a white background.
items.selection_reason: It shows the cross form alongside the reported early single-stroke form, making the graphic difference clear without implying a precise chronology between these depictions.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public domain as stated on the Commons file page.

limitations.text: The early stroke’s referent remains disputed. Proposals include a counting mark, needle, staff, joined palms, and knotted cord; the needle proposal does not establish the depicted object’s name or pronunciation or prove a borrowing into the numeral 十.
Both images are modern redrawings of historical script styles, not photographs of ancient artifacts; the seal-style image represents the Shuowen tradition rather than a securely dated artifact.
